explanation: The Almighty Creator who is the foundation of all things and has full power over nature, humanity, and history.
The term used to describe God's act of bringing the universe into existence from nothing by His will.
The messianic Savior who in Mark 3 exercises divine power through miracles, healings, and the casting out of evil spirits.
Twelve men Jesus chose specifically to be his closest disciples and witnesses to his deeds.
The evil power that stands in opposition to God and seeks to hinder God's kingdom, often by possessing people or causing suffering.
The divine rule where God's will is done on earth as it is in heaven, initiated through Jesus' ministry.
Human rebellion against God's laws and holy nature that leads to separation between humanity and God.
Divine intervention where Jesus removes sickness or suffering to demonstrate his power over death and destruction.
The activity in which Jesus denies himself something, often by taking on human weakness or enduring the accusations of others.
A title Jesus uses for himself that refers to his divine origin and his role as judge of the world at God's side.
